source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And the sages{H2450} and the Pharisees came{H935} to him, testing{H5254} him, that he might show{H3925} them some{H335} sign{H226} from the heavens{H8064}.

one_way_hebrew: מנסים (H5254, nasah) — the testing verb of Massah: 'you shall not test (תנסו) YHWH your God, as you tested him at Massah' (Deut 6:16; Exod 17:2,7). The sages come מנסים — doing to the Son exactly what the Torah forbids doing to God. Greek πειράζοντες translates the same charge.

The demand for an אות מהשמים ('sign from the heavens') is Deut 13:2-3's test-case: the sign-giver whose wonder comes to pass, sent to prove the heart. The Hebrew reader hears the statute behind the request.
greek_deviations: The challengers are החכמים והפרושים — 'the sages and the Pharisees' — where Greek Matthew has 'the Pharisees and Sadducees.' The Hebrew names the rabbinic estate (חכמים) alongside the Pharisees.
translation_notes: וילמדם — literally 'and that he might teach them' (למד, H3925); the sense is that they demanded he produce a sign for them to see, and Howard renders 'to show them.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:1): וילמדם] ילמדם ABEF; מהשמים] מן השמים A.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} them: Hypocrites{H2611}! You say{H559} in the evening{H6153}: Tomorrow{H4279} will be a clear{H6703} day{H3117}, because the heavens{H8064} are red{H122} —

one_way_hebrew: חנפים (H2611, chanef) — Job's word for the godless dissembler (Job 8:13; 13:16), the same word this text uses at 24:51; Greek ὑποκριταί ('stage-actors') is the theater metaphor, חנף the covenant one.
צח (H6703) — the shining-clear word of Isa 18:4 ('like a clear heat upon herbs') and Song 5:10; a Hebrew author's natural word for a cloudless day.
translation_notes: מחר — the scan of Howard's text reads מחר ('tomorrow'); the circulating transcription's מחת is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:2): יום צח יהיה] transposed (יהיה יום צח) in A; שהשמים] שרואים השמים G.
Greek Matthew 16:2b-3 (the weather-signs saying) is absent from many early Greek witnesses (א B and others); the Hebrew text carries it without question — no Shem Tov ms omits it.

verses.translation: and in the morning{H1242} you say{H559}: Today{H3117} it will rain{H4305}, for the heavens{H8064} are dark{H2821}. If so, you know{H3045} the judgment{H4941} of the appearances{H4758} of the heavens — but you do not know{H3045} the judgment{H4941} of the times{H2165}.

one_way_hebrew: משפט (H4941) — reading the sky and reading the times are both called a mishpat, a legal discernment: the Torah's judgment-word applied to the signs. Greek has merely 'you know how to discern (διακρίνειν) the face of the sky.'
הזמנים (H2165, zman) — the late-Biblical Hebrew time word (Esth 9:27,31; Neh 2:6), natural to a Hebrew author of this register; the same word this text uses at 24:23.
translation_notes: ימטיר — the scan of Howard's text reads ימטיר ('it will rain,' hiphil of מטר, H4305); the circulating transcription's ימטיף is a typo, corrected here.
א״כ — the ms writes the abbreviation א״כ for אם כן ('if so').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:3): ימטיר] ממטיר A; משפט²] + אותות A; מראים] מראית ABDEFG.

verses.translation: The seed{H2233} of evildoers{H7489} asks{H7592} for a sign{H226}, but a sign will not be given{H5414} them except the sign of Yonah{H3124} the prophet{H5030}. And then{H227} he separated{H6504} and went away{H1980}.

one_way_hebrew: זרע מרעים — 'a seed of evildoers': Isa 1:4's exact phrase (הוי גוי חטא... זרע מרעים) against Jerusalem's leaders. Greek Matthew has 'an evil and adulterous generation' (γενεὰ πονηρὰ καὶ μοιχαλίς); the Hebrew answers the sign-demand in Isaiah's own construct, aimed at the same class of men Isaiah aimed it at.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:4): להם] לו AEFG; נפרד] + מהם A ('separated from them' — Howard's English follows: 'he was separated (from them)'); נפרד והלך לו] omit EF.

verses.translation: And when Yeshua{H3442} was on the shore{H8193} of the sea{H3220}, he told{H559} his disciples{H8527} to prepare{H3559} bread{H3899}; and he entered{H3664} the ship{H5600} with his disciples, but his disciples forgot{H7911} and did not bring in{H3664} any bread.

one_way_hebrew: לספינה (H5600, sefinah) — Jonah's ship: ספינה occurs once in all of Scripture, in Jonah 1:5. One verse after 'the sign of Yonah the prophet' (v. 4), the Hebrew narrative boards Jonah's own vessel — a link no Greek reader can see, since Greek πλοῖον is the generic boat-word in both places.
בשפת הים — 'on the lip of the sea,' the idiom of Gen 22:17 and Exod 14:30 (שפת הים).
textual_notes: Greek 16:6-7 and the opening of v. 8 have no counterpart in the Shem Tov text: Howard's apparatus reads 'All MSS omit (hap.)' at 16:6-8a — an early copyist's eye skipped (haplography) and the whole Shem Tov family lost the leaven-warning and the disciples' reasoning; the text runs directly from v. 5 to v. 8, which Howard numbers 8b. The transcription marks 16:6 and 16:7 'vacant.'
Howard's apparatus (16:5): הים] + נפרד והלך לו EF (repeated from v. 4, printed between parentheses); לספינה] בספינה G; הכניסו] הכינו EF ('prepared').

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: You of little{H4592} understanding{H7922}, who think{H2803} that you have no{H369} bread{H3899}! Do you not remember{H2142} the five{H2568} loaves{H3603} and the four{H702} thousand{H505} men{H376}, and how many seahs{H5429} were left over{H7604}? Therefore{H3651} understand{H995} that I am not speaking{H1696} of the flint{H2496}, nor of the natural loaves{H3899}; but I am saying{H559} to you that you should keep yourselves apart{H7604} from the conduct of the Pharisees and the Sadducees.

one_way_hebrew: סאים (H5429, se'ah) — the loaves are measured in seahs, the Torah's own dry measure (Gen 18:6, 'three seahs of fine meal'); Greek has bare 'baskets.' A Hebrew author counts in seahs without thinking.

מהחלמיש (H2496, challamish) — 'the flint': Deut 8's word (Deut 8:15, 'who brought forth water for you out of the rock of flint'), from the very chapter that teaches 'man does not live by bread alone' (Deut 8:3). In a discourse about not meaning literal bread, the Hebrew reaches for Deut 8's own furniture — bread from heaven, water from flint.
greek_deviations: Where Greek Matthew spends four verses (16:9-12) on the two feedings ('the five loaves of the five thousand... the seven loaves of the four thousand') and the leaven, the Hebrew carries one condensed run that fuses the numbers — 'the five loaves and four thousand men' — and states the lesson directly: 'I am not speaking of the natural loaves... keep yourselves from the conduct of the Pharisees and the Sadducees.' Greek 'leaven' (ζύμη) has no counterpart word here; the text names the thing signified — their conduct (הנהגה).
translation_notes: שתשארו — 'that you be left apart / keep yourselves apart' (שאר, H7604); mss ABDEFG read שתשמרו ('that you beware of'), and Howard's English follows the variant: 'you should (beware) of the behavior.'
נשארו — the scan of Howard's text reads נשארו ('were left over'); the circulating transcription's נשער is a typo, corrected here.
הטבעיים ('natural') and מהנהגת ('from the conduct of') are medieval Hebrew terms with no biblical Strong's number.
textual_notes: Howard prints this verse as 8b (the first clause of Greek v. 8 fell in the haplography — see v. 5 note) and labels the run from ואין אתם זוכרים onward '9-12': one continuous passage standing where Greek Matthew has verses 9-12. There are no separate Shem Tov counterparts to 16:9, 10, 11, or 12.
Howard's apparatus (16:8b): שאין] אין A.

Howard's apparatus (16:9-12): מהחמשה] מהחמש AG; ככרות] דברות D; וארבע] וארבעת A; אלף] אלפים AEF; וכמה] כמה ABDEFG; ולכן] לכן G; מהחלמיש וגם] omit ABDEFG (Howard's English follows the majority: 'I am not speaking of natural loaves'); שתשארו] שתשמרו ABDEFG; לכם] omit A.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} went out{H3318} to the land{H776} of Suria'ah and the land of Philoph, called{H7121} Philibos, and he asked{H7592} his disciples{H8527}, saying{H559}: What{H4100} do the sons{H1121} of man{H120} say about me?

greek_deviations: Greek Matthew has 'the district of Caesarea Philippi'; the Hebrew reads 'the land of Suria'ah and the land of Philoph, called Philibos' — the region named as two lands, with the ruler's name (Philip the tetrarch) attached to his territory and glossed with its Greek form. Mss ABDEF add a לעז gloss identifying סוריא״ה as Cesarea ('in the foreign tongue, Cesaria'), which Howard's English renders '(that is, Caesarea)' — again a Hebrew text being annotated with the church's place-names for its readers.

The question is asked about בני אדם — 'the sons of man' — where Greek asks what men say 'about the Son of Man.' In the Hebrew, the title בן אדם is not in the question; it is the askers who are בני אדם.
translation_notes: The printed text points the foreign names (סוּרִיאָ״ה, פִילִיב״וֹס) to guide pronunciation; the vowel points are stripped here, and the transcription's point-broken spacing (סוּרִ יאָ ״ה, פִ ילִ יב״וֹס) is repaired against the scan.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ע״א (Perek 71) begins here.

Howard's apparatus (16:13): סוריאה] + בלעז שישאריאה B ('in the foreign tongue, Cesaria'), with similar la'az glosses in ADEF; וארץ] ארץ B; פילוף נקרא] omit H; פיליבוס] פיליפוש ABDEF, פיליפוס G; מה] + הם D.

verses.translation: And they said{H559} to him: Some say{H559} he is Yochanan{H3110} the Immerser{H2881}, and some say he is Eliyahu{H452}, and some Yirmeyahu{H3414}, or one{H259} of the prophets{H5030}.

one_way_hebrew: המטביל — 'the Immerser,' from טבל (H2881), the verb of Naaman's sevenfold dipping in the Jordan (2 Kgs 5:14). Greek βαπτιστής is a Greek coinage; the Hebrew title is built on the Tanakh's own immersion verb.
translation_notes: או א״ — the ms abbreviates אחד ('one') as א״; the scan reads או א״ ('or one of'), and the circulating transcription's ור א is corrected accordingly.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:14): whole verse omitted in EF; אומרים²] omit G; אליהו] אליה BH; ירמיהו] ירמיה BH.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to them: And you{H859}, what{H4100} do you say{H559} about me?

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:15): whole verse omitted in EF; ואתם מה] מה אתם D; מה] + אתם G.

verses.translation: And Shimon{H8095}, called{H7121} Petros, answered{H6030} and said{H559}: You are Mashiach{H4899} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, Kristo — the Son{H1121} of the living{H2416} Elohim{H430}, who has come{H935} into this{H2088} world{H5769}.

one_way_hebrew: The confession's own word is משיח, and the text glosses it לעז קריסט״ו — 'in the foreign tongue, Kristo' — for readers who knew the church's vocabulary. A translator FROM Greek would be rendering χριστός and would never need to gloss his source-word with itself; the gloss runs the other way, exactly as with evangeli (24:14) and Antichristos (24:15): the Hebrew word is native, the Greek word is the visitor.
greek_deviations: The confession ends with a clause absent from Greek Matthew: שבאתה בזה העולם — 'who has come into this world.' Greek Matthew stops at 'the Son of the living God'; the fuller form matches Martha's confession in John 11:27 ('You are the Messiah, the Son of God, who is coming into the world'). The Hebrew Matthew and John share a confession formula that Greek Matthew lacks.
textual_notes: אלקים — the ms uses the reverent ק-spelling of אלהים (so throughout this text).

The printed text points קְרִיסט״וֹ to guide pronunciation of the foreign word; the points are stripped here and the transcription's broken spacing repaired against the scan, which also reads פייט״רוס (the transcription's פיית״רוס is a typo, corrected here).
Howard's apparatus (16:16): פייטרוס] פיטרו A, פיטרוש BDEFG, פיטרוס C; ויאמר] omit H; משיח] המשיח H; לעז קריסטו] omit H; קריסטו] קרישטו ADG, קריסטוס EF; אלקים] אלים A; שבאתה] שבאת ACDEFGH.
The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads simply 'You are Mashiach, the Son of the living El,' without the la'az gloss and without 'who has come into this world.'

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to him: Happy are you{H835}, Shimon{H8095} bar{H1247} Yonah{H3124}, for flesh{H1320} and blood{H1818} has not revealed{H1540} it to you, but my Father{H1} who is in the heavens{H8064}.

one_way_hebrew: אשריך — the Psalter's beatitude form addressed to a person (Ps 128:2; Deut 33:29, אשריך ישראל). Greek μακάριος εἶ translates it.
שבשר ודם — basar va-dam, 'flesh and blood': the rabbinic Hebrew idiom for mortal man as against Heaven (מלך בשר ודם of a thousand midrashim). Greek σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα is a calque of this Hebrew pair.

בר יונה — בר (H1247) is the Aramaic 'son' embedded in a Hebrew sentence, exactly how patronymics were actually borne; the Greek text itself preserves it untranslated (Βαριωνᾶ), a fossil of the Semitic original.
translation_notes: ויאמרו — the base ms writes a plural form where the sense is singular ('and he said'); mss BCDEG read ויאמר and AFH the abbreviated ויאמ׳ — the base spelling is a copyist's slip of the common kind.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:17): ויאמרו] ויאמ׳ AFH, ויאמר BCDEG; בר] בן H; שבשר] שבשה G; שבשר ודם] שב״ו AH (the pair abbreviated); לך] omit G.

verses.translation: And I say{H559} to you: you are a stone{H68}, and I will build{H1129} upon you{H5921} my house{H1004} of prayer{H8605}; and the gates{H8179} of Gehinnom{H1516} will not prevail{H3201} against you{H5048}.

one_way_hebrew: אתה אבן ואני אבנה — 'you are a STONE (even) and I will BUILD (evneh)': the wordplay is complete in Hebrew, where the verb בנה shares its consonants with אבן (cf. Gen 16:2 אבנה; Ps 118:22, 'the stone the builders rejected'). Greek Πέτρος/πέτρα mirrors the noun but the verb οἰκοδομήσω has no share in the pun — and Greek must switch genders (Petros/petra) where the Hebrew simply says 'you are a stone... upon you.'

בית תפלתי — 'my house of prayer': Isa 56:7 verbatim (ושמחתים בבית תפלתי... כי ביתי בית תפלה יקרא לכל העמים). Where Greek Matthew has ἐκκλησία ('church' — its only occurrence in the gospels with 21:17's), the Hebrew quotes Isaiah's own name for the gathered house open to all peoples. A back-translator from ἐκκλησία would write קהל; only a Hebrew author writes Isaiah's בית תפלתי.
שערי גהינם — built like שערי שאול, 'the gates of Sheol' (Isa 38:10; cf. Job 38:17, 'the gates of death'): the underworld as a walled city whose gates cannot hold the besieger.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew builds upon Shimon himself — ואני אבנה עליך, 'and I will build UPON YOU' — with no stone/rock switch: Greek's 'you are Πέτρος and upon this πέτρᾳ' introduces a second term the Hebrew does not have (ms A reads ועל זאת האבן אבנה, 'upon this stone I will build,' assimilating toward the Greek).

The gates will not prevail נגדך — 'against YOU' (singular, Shimon) — where all Greek manuscripts read 'against IT' (αὐτῆς, the assembly). No Greek witness has 'against you'; the Hebrew families do (the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew likewise reads 'the doors of Gei-Hinnom will not prevail against you,' even while it reads 'upon this stone I will build my assembly' in the first half). The promise here is to the man, not the institution.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:18): ואני אבנה עליך] ועל זאת האבן אבנה A, ועליך אבנה H; גהינם] גיהנם BD; נגדך] נגדה A, לך G.

verses.translation: For I will give{H5414} you the keys{H4668} of the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064}; and all{H3605} that you bind{H7194} on earth{H776} will be bound in heaven, and all that you loose{H5425} on earth will be loosed in heaven.

one_way_hebrew: מפתחות — the keys: Isa 22:22's investiture scene ('and the key of the house of David I will lay upon his shoulder; he shall open, and none shall shut'), the Tanakh's one giving-of-the-key to a steward set over the house.

תקשור... תתיר — bind and loose (קשר, H7194; התיר from נתר, H5425) — the halakhic idiom for forbidding and permitting (אסר/התיר), the working vocabulary of a Hebrew court. Greek δέω/λύω translates the idiom; in Hebrew it is simply how legal authority speaks.
translation_notes: בארץ — the scan of Howard's text reads תקשור בארץ; the circulating transcription's מארץ is a typo, corrected here.
The 'you' of the keys, the binding, and the loosing is singular throughout — the grant is to Shimon, continuing v. 18.
textual_notes: No variants recorded in Howard's apparatus for this verse — the reading is uniform across the Shem Tov mss.

verses.translation: Then{H227} he commanded{H6680} his disciples{H8527} not{H1077} to say{H559} that he is Mashiach{H4899}.

textual_notes: No variants recorded in Howard's apparatus for this verse.

verses.translation: From then onward Yeshua{H3442} began{H2490} to reveal{H1540} to his disciples{H8527} that he must{H6878} go{H1980} to Yerushalayim{H3389} and bear{H5375} the wrong{H5766} of many{H7227} from the priests{H3548} and the elders{H2205} of the people{H5971}, until they kill{H2026} him — and on the third{H7992} day{H3117} he will arise{H6965}.

one_way_hebrew: ולשאת עול רבים — 'to BEAR the wrong of MANY': the vocabulary of the Servant (Isa 53:11-12 — 'my righteous servant shall justify MANY, for he shall BEAR their iniquities... he BORE the sin of MANY,' נשא + רבים). Greek has 'suffer many things' (πολλὰ παθεῖν) — quantity of sufferings, not bearing for the many; the Hebrew carries Isaiah's freight.

ויום השלישי יקום — 'on the third day he will ARISE' (קום, H6965, active): Hos 6:2's promise ('on the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live before him'). Greek ἐγερθῆναι is passive 'be raised'; the Hebrew stands with Hosea's wording.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק ע״ב (Perek 72) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (16:21): לגלות] omit G; עול] על EF ('the yoke of many' — the same consonants unpointed read either 'wrong' or 'yoke'); ויום] וביום A.

verses.translation: And Petros took him{H3947} aside, between him and himself{H996}, and began{H2490} to rebuke{H3198} him, saying{H559}: Far be it{H2486} from you — that it should be{H1961} so{H3651} for you, my lord{H113}!

one_way_hebrew: חלילה לך — Abraham's own protest formula before the Judge of all the earth (Gen 18:25, חלילה לך). Greek ἵλεώς σοι ('mercy to you') is the LXX's stock rendering of exactly this Hebrew interjection — the Greek text is translating a Hebrew idiom that stands here in the original.
בינו לבינו — 'between him and himself,' the native בין...לבין construction (Gen 26:28); Greek has only 'took him aside.'
translation_notes: אדו׳ — the ms abbreviates אדון/אדוני ('my lord') with a geresh.
The scan reads בינו לבינו (once each); the circulating transcription doubles בינו — corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:22): ויקחוהו] ויקחהו ADEFG; פייטרוס] פיטרו A, פיטרוס B, פיטרוש DEFG; והתחיל להוכיח לאמר] ויאמר לו G; להוכיח] להוכיחו A (Howard's English: 'began to rebuke (him)'); להיות...אדו׳] אדון להיות לך G; לך²] omit C; כן אדו׳] transposed in A.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} turned{H7725} and looked{H5027} at him, and said{H559} to him: Go{H1980}, satan{H7854}! Do not rebel against{H4784} my mouth{H6310}, for you do not recognize{H5234} the word{H1697} of El{H410}, but only the words of man{H120}.

one_way_hebrew: לא תמרה פי — 'do not rebel against my mouth': the Torah's own rebellion idiom, מרה את פי (Num 20:24, 'because you rebelled against my mouth at the waters of Meribah'; 1 Sam 12:14-15; 1 Kgs 13:21,26). The base text applies the idiom of rebelling against YHWH's mouth to rebelling against Yeshua's word. Greek has nothing of it.
השטן (H7854) — with the article, 'the adversary': the Hebrew term of Job 1-2 and Zech 3:1-2, a role-word (accuser, opposer), here laid on Petros in the moment he opposes.
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew adds 'you are a stumbling-block (σκάνδαλον) to me' — the clause is absent from the Hebrew, which instead has the Torah idiom 'do not rebel against my mouth.' And where Greek has 'you mind (φρονεῖς) not the things of God,' the Hebrew has 'you do not RECOGNIZE (מכיר) the word of El' — a failure of discernment, not of preference.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:23): לו] omit D; פי] בי ABDEF ('do not rebel against ME' — Howard's English follows the variant: 'do not disobey (me)'); שאינך] שאתה אינך ABDEFG.

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} spoke{H1696} to his disciples{H8527}: Whoever desires{H7521} to come{H935} after{H310} me, let him despise{H959} himself{H6106} and take{H3947} the warp{H8359} and woof{H6154} — that is to say, let him offer{H7126} himself to death{H4194} — and come after me.

one_way_hebrew: השתי וערב — 'the warp and woof': Leviticus 13's own fixed pair for the crossed threads of a garment (שתי/ערב nine times in Lev 13:48-59), which medieval Hebrew used to name a cross-shape without borrowing the church's word. Greek σταυρόν ('cross') is one word; the Hebrew reaches for the Torah's weaving pair.

The text then glosses ITSELF: ר״ל ('that is to say') שקרב עצמו למיתה — 'that he offer himself to death.' The explanatory abbreviation ר״ל is the scribe helping Hebrew readers over the idiom, exactly the annotation pattern of the la'az glosses (24:14-15; 16:16): the Hebrew is the text being read, not a translation being made.
שקרב (H7126) — the sacrificial verb (hiphil of קרב, 'bring near as an offering,' Lev 1:2): to take the warp-and-woof is to bring oneself near to death as a korban.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:24): the opening is rewritten in G (אז לקח ישו את תלמידיו ואמר להם); יבזה] + את ADG; ויקח] ויקרב EF; את] omit AG; שקרב] שיקרב ABD.

verses.translation: Everyone{H3605} who desires{H7521} to save{H3467} his soul{H5315} will lose{H6} it for my sake{H1157}, and he who loses{H6} his life{H2416} in this world for my sake will save{H3467} his soul for the life{H2416} of the world to come.

one_way_hebrew: בעה״ז... העה״ב — 'in this world... the world to come': the rabbinic pair olam ha-zeh / olam ha-ba, written in the ms as standard Hebrew abbreviations (בעה״ז, העה״ב). Greek 16:25 has neither term. Only a text living inside Jewish eschatological vocabulary abbreviates it; a back-translator from Greek would have nothing to abbreviate.
יושיע... להושיע (H3467, yasha) — the saving verb that is the root of the name ישו״ע, as at 24:13.
greek_deviations: The Greek verse turns on 'finding' and 'losing' one life; the Hebrew states the exchange in full: lose life in THIS WORLD, save the soul for THE LIFE OF THE WORLD TO COME. The two-worlds frame is in the text itself, not the commentary.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:25): בשבילי] omit D; נפשו] את נפשו G.

verses.translation: What{H4100} profit{H1215} is there for a man{H120} if he gains{H7304} the whole{H3605} world{H5769}, if his soul{H5315} is lost{H6} forever{H5703}? And what good{H2896} exchange{H8545} does the man make, if for things{H1697} that now are{H1933} and perish he gives{H5414} his soul{H5315} to the judgment{H1779} of Gehinnom{H1516}?

one_way_hebrew: מה בצע — 'what profit?': Judah's question over Joseph (Gen 37:26, מה בצע כי נהרג את אחינו) and the psalmist's (Ps 30:10, מה בצע בדמי). The Hebrew asks the Tanakh's own cost-question.

תמורה (H8545) — the exchange-word of Job 28:15-17 ('it cannot be gotten for gold... the EXCHANGE of it shall not be for vessels of fine gold') and Lev 27:10,33 — what may and may not be swapped. Greek ἀντάλλαγμα translates it.
לדין גהינם — 'the judgment of Gehinnom': din Gehinnom, the standing rabbinic term for the sentence of the grave-fire. Greek Matthew has no judgment-clause here at all; the Hebrew names the court.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew adds לעד ('his soul is lost FOREVER') and defines the bad bargain: 'things that now are and perish' (ההווים והנפסדים) traded for the soul — the transient/eternal contrast is explicit where the Greek only implies it.
translation_notes: ההווים ('the things that now are,' from הוה) and והנפסדים ('and that perish,' medieval nifsad) are the philosophical Hebrew of the Even Bochan's own century — the author writes his generation's Hebrew, as any living author does.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:26): את] omit ABDEFG; ואיזה] ואיזו A; בעד הדברים] בדברים EF; והנפסדים] הנפסדים AB; נפשו²] לנפשו EF.

verses.translation: For the Son{H1121} of El{H410} will come{H935} in the glory{H3519} of his Father{H1} who is in the heavens{H8064}, with his messengers{H4397}, to repay{H7725} every man{H376} according to his work{H4659}.

one_way_hebrew: להשיב לכל איש כמפעלו — Prov 24:12's clause ('and shall he not RENDER to every man according to his WORKS?' — והשיב לאדם כפעלו; cf. Ps 62:13). The Hebrew stands on the proverb's own verb and noun; Greek ἀποδώσει ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν πρᾶξιν αὐτοῦ translates it.
greek_deviations: בן האל — 'the Son of EL' — where Greek Matthew reads 'the Son of MAN (ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου) will come in the glory of his Father.' The Hebrew gives the coming-in-glory to the Son of El by name; v. 28 does the same with בן אלוה. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew likewise reads a divine title here ('El will come with the glory of his Father') — the Hebrew families stand together against the Greek.
translation_notes: בכבד — the ms spells בכבוד ('in the glory of') defectively.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:27): שבשמים] אשר בשמים ABDEFG; עם מלאכיו] omit A; כמפעלו] כפעלו ABDEF, כפעולו G.

verses.translation: Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you: there are{H3426} some of those standing{H5975} here{H6311} who will not taste{H2938} death{H4194} until{H5704} they see{H7200} the Son{H1121} of Eloah{H433} coming{H935} in his kingdom{H4438}.

one_way_hebrew: יטעמו מות — 'taste death': the Hebrew idiom behind the Greek's γεύσωνται θανάτου; טעם (H2938) is Jonathan's tasting verb ('I did but taste a little honey... and lo, I must die,' 1 Sam 14:43) and the idiom te'ame mita of the rabbis.
greek_deviations: בן אלוה — 'the Son of ELOAH coming in his kingdom' — where Greek Matthew reads 'the Son of MAN coming in his kingdom.' Eloah (H433) is the singular divine name of Job and Deut 32:15. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads the same ('until they have seen the Son of Eloah coming in his kingdom') — both Hebrew families against the Greek, twice in two verses (see v. 27).
translation_notes: מהעומדים — the scan of Howard's text reads מהעומדים ('of those standing'); the circulating transcription's מהעימדים is a typo, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (16:28): שיראו] + את ABDEF; אלוה] האלים A, האלוה G; בא] omit BEF; יטעמו] + טעם EF.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 16 in the Shem Tov Hebrew carries its heaviest differences exactly where the chapter carries its heaviest doctrine. (1) 16:18 reads 'you are a STONE (אבן) and I will build UPON YOU my HOUSE OF PRAYER (בית תפלתי)' — Isa 56:7's own phrase where Greek has ἐκκλησία ('church'); the even/evneh wordplay is complete in Hebrew with no Petros/petra gender-switch; and the gates of Gehinnom 'will not prevail AGAINST YOU' (singular) — a reading no Greek manuscript has, but which the Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew shares. Ms A assimilates to the Greek ('upon this stone'). (2) 16:19's bind/loose is the rabbinic forbid/permit idiom (תקשור/תתיר), with Isa 22:22's key behind the מפתחות. (3) 16:16's confession is glossed from inside — 'You are Mashiach, לעז Kristo' — and ends 'who has come into this world,' a clause Greek Matthew lacks but John 11:27 has. (4) 16:24 has no 'cross': the disciple takes 'the warp and woof' (שתי וערב, Lev 13's weaving pair), and the text glosses itself — ר״ל, 'that is to say, that he offer himself to death.' (5) 16:27-28 read 'the Son of EL will come in the glory of his Father' and 'the Son of ELOAH coming in his kingdom' where Greek reads 'Son of Man' both times — and Vat. Ebr. 100 agrees with the Hebrew both times. (6) 16:4 answers the sign-demand with Isa 1:4's זרע מרעים ('seed of evildoers'), and v. 5 boards Jonah's own ספינה (Jonah 1:5, its only occurrence in Scripture) one verse after 'the sign of Yonah.' (7) 16:6-8a fell out of the entire ms family by haplography (Howard: 'All MSS omit (hap.)'; 16:7 stands 'vacant'), and 16:9-12 survive as one condensed run Howard labels '9-12.' (8) 16:21 has the Servant's vocabulary — 'bear the wrong of many' (Isa 53:11-12) — and Hosea's 'on the third day he will ARISE' (Hos 6:2). (9) 16:23 rebukes with the Torah idiom 'do not rebel against my mouth' (Num 20:24) and lacks the stumbling-block clause. (10) 16:25 states the exchange in the rabbis' own abbreviated pair — this world (בעה״ז) against the world to come (העה״ב). Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 13 (Perek 71) and 21 (Perek 72).
